record.original_question: What is a general classification or characterization of geodetic graphs, where a graph is geodetic when every pair of distinct vertices is connected by a unique shortest path (a unique geodesic)?

evidence.quote: A geodetic graph is one in which every pair of its vertices has a unique path of shortest length.
As mentioned before, Ore [9] posed the question of characterizing geodetic graphs, which is still unresolved.

Characterization, enumeration and the general classification of geodetic graphs are open problems that have become a very important research topic due to the fact that geodetic graphs can be applied to the solution of other relevant problems in computer science [1, 2, 3].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A simple, connected, undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ is called geodetic if for every pair of distinct vertices $u,v \in V$ there is exactly one shortest path (geodesic) joining $u$ and $v$ in $G$. Familiar examples of geodetic graphs include all trees, all complete graphs, and all odd cycles.

Provide a general structural classification (equivalently, a structural characterization) of all geodetic graphs: namely, give necessary and sufficient combinatorial/structural conditions on a finite simple connected graph $G$ that determine whether $G$ is geodetic, expressed in terms of the description of its constituent substructures (such as the arrangement of complete subgraphs, paths, and cycles contained within $G$).
artifact.status_search_result: Ore posed the problem of characterizing geodetic graphs in his 1962 book, and the problem of providing a general structural classification of geodetic graphs remains unresolved. Although recognition can be done in polynomial time and partial characterizations exist (e.g. for diameter 2, or in terms of embedded even graphs in a 2026 arXiv preprint), no complete structural characterization is known. Wikipedia and recent literature confirm the problem is still open more than sixty years after Ore raised it.
